_about: Everything the space buddy knows and says when it talks with the child. The buddy is NOT an AI: it looks for words in what the child types (patterns) and answers ONLY with the sentences in this file (or the ones a grown-up added in 'Teach my buddy'). Nothing the child says is saved or sent - except a worrying message (the 'safety' list), which goes ONLY to the child's grown-up and teacher. See CONTENT_GUIDE.md section 13 for how to add things.

settings._helpline: Optional: one sentence about a children's helpline in your country, shown when a child asks who they can talk to. Example (UK): 'You can also call Childline on 0800 1111. It's free.' Leave it empty to only say 'a grown-up you trust'.

patterns: wants to know where i live
replies: Thank you for telling me. 💜 People online should never ask for your photos, where you live, or to meet you.
I'm glad you told me. 💜 Don't send anything or tell them where you live.

safety.title: Might be lost
replies: Oh no! 💜 If you are lost, stay where you are. Look for a safe grown-up, like a police officer, a shop worker, or a mom with kids, and say: “I'm lost. Can you help me?”

safety.title: A secret that may not be safe
patterns: made me promise not to tell
replies: Thank you for telling me. 💜 Some secrets are OK, like a birthday surprise. 🎁 But secrets that feel bad, scary or confusing should always be told to a grown-up you trust. You won't be in trouble.

safety.title: Someone did something they did not like
replies: Thank you for telling me. 💜 Your body belongs to you. You can say “Stop, I don't like that!” And it's always OK to tell a grown-up.

safety.title: Being bullied or teased
replies: I'm sorry that happened. 💜 Nobody should be mean to you. It is not your fault, and you are great just the way you are.
That's not OK. 💜 You don't deserve that. You are a great kid.

safety.title: Very unhappy about themselves
replies: I'm sorry you feel that way. 💜 But I know something: you are NOT stupid or bad. You are kind and you are important.
That sounds like a really heavy feeling. 💜 You matter, and you are loved, even when it doesn't feel like it.

Owls can turn their heads really far, almost all the way around! 🦉
Cats sleep for about 12 to 16 hours a day. 😴🐱
Every dog's nose print is different, like your fingerprint! 🐶
Cheetahs are the fastest animals on land. They can run as fast as a car on the highway! 🐆
Elephants are the biggest animals on land, and they can't jump! 🐘
Penguins can't fly, but they are amazing swimmers! 🐧
Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day! 🐨
A baby kangaroo is called a joey. 🦘
Bees do a little dance to tell other bees where the flowers are! 🐝

topics.name: car
topics.title: Cars
facts: The very first car could only go about as fast as a bicycle! 🚲
Race cars can go faster than 300 kilometres an hour! 🏎️💨
Electric cars run on big batteries, like a giant phone battery! 🔋🚗
Tires are black because of a special black powder that makes them strong. ⚫
A car has about 30,000 parts! 🔩
Monster truck tires can be about as tall as a grown-up! 🛻
In some countries, like the UK and Japan, cars drive on the left side of the road. ⬅️
Fire trucks carry ladders, hoses and lots of water to help put out fires. 🚒
Some race cars push down on the road so hard that they could drive upside down on a tunnel ceiling, in theory! 🤯
Diggers can lift heavy rocks with their big arm and bucket. 🏗️
A big bus can carry more than 50 people at once! 🚌
Seatbelts keep you safe in a car. Always click it! 🔒

topics.name: space
topics.title: Space
facts: Jupiter is the biggest planet. More than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it! 🪐
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus! 🤯
Footprints on the Moon can stay there for millions of years, because there is no wind. 👣🌙
The Sun is a star! ☀️ It's the closest star to us.
Saturn is so light that it could float in a giant bathtub! 🛁🪐
Astronauts on the space station see about 16 sunrises every day! 🌅
Mars is red because its dust has rust in it! 🔴
Space is super quiet. There is no air to carry sound! 🤫
Neptune has the fastest winds of all the planets! 💨
Astronauts get a little taller in space! 📏
Scientists think there are more stars in space than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches! ✨
The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth, about 4 centimetres every year. 🌙

topics.name: dinosaur
topics.title: Dinosaurs
facts: Some dinosaurs had feathers! 🪶
Birds are living dinosaurs! 🐦🦖
A T. rex had teeth as long as bananas! 🍌🦖
Dinosaurs lived on Earth for more than 150 million years! ⏳
The biggest dinosaurs were as long as about three buses! 🚌🚌🚌
Velociraptors were only about the size of a turkey! 🦃
Triceratops had three horns on its face. 🦕
Dinosaurs hatched from eggs, like birds! 🥚
A scientist who studies dinosaur fossils is called a paleontologist. 🔍
Stegosaurus had big plates on its back and spikes on its tail. 🦕
Some dinosaurs were as small as a chicken! 🐔
The word “dinosaur” means “terrible lizard”. 🦎

topics.name: train
topics.title: Trains
facts: Some trains float above the track using magnets! 🧲🚄
Bullet trains in Japan can go about 300 kilometres an hour! 🚅
The first steam trains for passengers started about 200 years ago! 🚂
Steam trains burn coal to boil water. The steam pushes the wheels! 💨
London has the oldest underground train in the world. It opened in 1863! 🚇
The longest train trip in one country crosses Russia and takes about a week! 🗺️
Freight trains can be very long, sometimes more than 100 cars long! 🚃
Train tracks are made of steel, so they can hold very heavy trains. 🛤️
In some countries, a train driver is called an engineer! 🧑‍🔧
Trams are trains that drive on tracks in the street. 🚋

topics.name: ocean
topics.title: The ocean
facts: Most of planet Earth is covered by oceans! 🌊
Seahorse dads carry the babies! 🐠
Sharks lived on Earth before there were trees! 🦈🌳
A sea star (starfish) can grow back a lost arm! ⭐
Dolphins sleep with half of their brain at a time! 🐬
Jellyfish don't have a brain! 🌊
Some deep-sea fish make their own light! ✨🐟
The deepest place in the ocean is deeper than Mount Everest is tall! 🏔️
Clownfish live in sea anemones, which are like soft, wiggly homes. 🐠
The blue whale is the biggest animal that ever lived, bigger than any dinosaur! 🐋
Octopuses can change colour to hide! 🐙
Sea turtles travel very far across the ocean, and many come back to the beach where they hatched! 🐢

jokes.q: Why did the cow go to space?
What do you call a sleeping dinosaur?
What do planets like to read?
How do you throw a party in space?
What did the ocean say to the beach?
Why was the math book sad?
What do you call a bear with no teeth?
Why did the teddy bear say no to dessert?
What do you call a dog that does magic?
Where do astronauts park their spaceships?
What's an astronaut's favourite key on the keyboard?
Why did the robot go on vacation?
What do you call a train that sneezes?
Why did the cookie go to the doctor?
What has four wheels and flies?

help.title: I want to join a game
help.intro: Joining a game can feel scary. You can do it! 💪
steps: Watch the game for a little bit. What are the rules? 👀
Walk over. You can smile if you want to. 🙂
Ask: “Can I play too?” 🙋
If they say yes: have fun! 🎉 If they say no: that's OK. Find another game or another kid. 💜
say: That looks fun! Can I join?
Can I have the next turn?

help.title: I don't know what to say
help.intro: Starting to talk is tricky for lots of people. Here's a trick! ✨
steps: Say hi and their name. 👋
Ask a question, like “What do you like to play?” ❓
Listen to their answer. 👂
Tell them something about you too. 💬
It's OK if it feels hard. A little “hi” is a great start! 🌟
say: What do you like to play?

help.title: I want to make a friend
help.intro: Friends are great! Here's how friendships start. 🌱
steps: Find someone who likes the same things as you. 🦕🚂
Say hi, and ask what they like. 👋
Play together, share, and take turns. 🧩
Be kind, and say nice things. 💜
Friendships grow slowly, like a plant. Keep trying! 🌱
say: Do you want to play with me?
help.outro: Maybe you can play with {friend} soon! 🌟

help.title: Someone is mean to me
help.intro: Nobody should be mean to you. It's not your fault. 💜
steps: Say in a strong voice: “Stop! I don't like that.” ✋
Walk away to a safe place. 🚶
Tell a grown-up: a teacher, your mom or dad. 🗣️
Stay close to friends or a grown-up. 👫
If it happens again, tell a grown-up again. You are brave! 🦸
say: I'm going to tell a teacher.

help.title: It's too loud, too much
help.intro: When everything is too much, your brain needs a break. That's OK! 🤫
steps: Cover your ears or put on headphones. 🎧
Tell a grown-up: “It's too much. I need a break.” 🗣️
Go to a quiet place. 🤫
Breathe slowly: in through your nose… out through your mouth. 🌬️
Do something calming, like squeezing a soft toy. 🧸
say: It's too loud. I need a break.
help.outro: Your grown-up says {calm} helps you, too. 💜

help.title: I feel so angry
help.intro: Angry feelings are OK. Hurting people or things is not OK. Here's what helps! 🌋
steps: STOP. Freeze like a statue. 🗿
Take 3 big, slow breaths. 🌬️
Count to 10, slowly. 🔢
Squeeze a pillow or push against a wall. 💪
Use words: “I feel angry because…” 💬

help.title: My friend is sad
help.intro: You want to help someone who is sad. That's so kind! 💜
steps: Look at their face and body. Are they crying or looking down? 👀
Ask: “Are you OK?” 💬
Listen to what they say. 👂
Ask: “Can I help?” or “Do you want to play?” 🤝
If they want to be alone, that's OK. You can tell a grown-up too. 💜
say: Do you want to play with me?

help.title: I made a mistake
steps: Stop and take a breath. 🌬️
Say sorry: “I'm sorry I…” 💬
Ask: “How can I make it better?” 🤝
Learn from it. Next time, you'll know! 🧠
say: How can I make it better?

help.title: Are they joking?
help.intro: Sometimes people say things they don't really mean, as a joke. It can be confusing! 🤔
steps: Look at their face: are they smiling or laughing? 😄
Listen to their voice: does it sound silly or different? 🔊
Think: does it make sense? “Oh great, it's raining!” might mean they're NOT happy. ☔
Not sure? Ask! “Are you joking?” That's a smart question. 🙋

help.title: I'm going somewhere new
help.intro: New places can feel big and strange. Here's how to get ready! 🗺️
steps: Ask a grown-up what will happen there. 📋
Look at pictures of the place, if you can. 🖼️
Bring something that makes you feel calm, like a toy. 🧸
Find a grown-up there who can help you. 🙋
It's OK to feel nervous. It gets easier! 🌟

help.title: Someone is too close to me
help.intro: Your body belongs to you. You can say NO. 💜
steps: Say: “Please give me some space.” ✋
Take a step back. 👣
If they don't stop, say “STOP!” in a strong voice. 🛑
Tell a grown-up you trust. It's never your fault. 💜
You can say “No thank you” to hugs. A high five is OK too! ✋
say: Can we do a high five instead?

help.title: It's hard to wait my turn
help.intro: Waiting is hard for everyone! Here are some tricks. ⏳
steps: Ask: “Can I have a turn after you?” 🙋
Count slowly while you wait. 🔢
Do something else while you wait, like humming a song. 🎵
When it's your turn: enjoy it! 🎉 Then give the next person a turn too. 🔄
say: Can I have a turn after you?

faces.title: Guess my face
faces.about: I make a face. You guess the feeling!
wrong: Hmm, not quite! 💜 Here's a hint: {hint}

rounds.hint: My mouth goes up in a smile!
My mouth goes down, and there's a tear.
My eyebrows go down, and my mouth is tight.
My eyes are big and my mouth is a round O!
A HUGE smile. I can't wait!
My tongue is out and I'm winking!

kindOrNot.title: Kind or not kind?
kindOrNot.about: I say something. Is it kind?
ask: Is this kind or not kind?

rounds.why: Asking nicely is kind! 💜
That could really hurt someone's feelings. 💔
Saying nice things makes people smile! 😊

rounds.text: Haha, you fell! You're so clumsy.
rounds.why: Laughing at someone who got hurt is not kind. You could ask “Are you OK?” 💜

rounds.text: Are you OK? Do you need help?
rounds.why: Checking on someone is super kind! 🤝

rounds.text: You can't play. Only cool kids can play.
rounds.why: Leaving people out hurts. Everyone can play! 💜
Saying thank you is kind! 🌟
Those words hurt a lot. 💔 Kind words help everyone feel safe.
Taking turns is fair and kind! 🔄
You could say “I have another idea!” instead. 💡
Saying sorry is kind and brave! 💜

rounds.text: Stop flapping your hands, it's weird.
rounds.why: Hand flapping is OK! Everyone's body moves in its own way. 🙌
Cheering for others is kind! 🎉

rounds.text: Do you want to sit with me?
rounds.why: Inviting someone is so kind! 🪑

wouldYouRather.title: Would you rather
wouldYouRather.about: Pick one, then ask me back!
picked: {choice}! Great pick! 😊 Now ask me back: “What about you?”
praise: +1 🍬 Great job asking me back! That's what good friends do. ⭐

rounds.why: I'd fly up to the stars! ✨
Ice cream on a moon rock! 🌙
The view of Earth is amazing! 🌍
It could keep me warm in space! 🔥
I love building sand rockets! 🚀
Zoom! I'd race comets! ☄️
I'd ask cats why they love boxes! 📦
Rockets go to space, my home! 🛰️
A tower all the way to the clouds! ☁️

rounds.a: Be a dinosaur for a day 🦖
rounds.b: Be a cat for a day 🐱
rounds.why: So many naps! 😴
Pancakes at night are the best! 🌙
I want to see real dinosaurs! 🦕

whatWouldYouSay.title: What would you say?
whatWouldYouSay.about: Practice what to say in real life.

rounds.situation: A friend shows you their new toy.

options.reply: That's a great thing to say! Your friend feels happy. 😊
Hmm, that might make your friend feel sad. 💜 You could say something nice about their toy.
That's OK! You could also say “Cool!” to show you care. 😊
Yes! That will make them smile! 🎂
Hmm, that could feel unkind on their special day. 💜 “Happy birthday” is a nice thing to say.
That's OK if it feels hard. A small “Happy birthday” can make someone's day! 🎈

rounds.situation: A kid is crying on the playground.

options.reply: That's so kind! Asking shows you care. 💜
Hmm, that would make them feel worse. 💜 Everybody cries sometimes.
Getting a grown-up is a smart way to help! 🌟

rounds.situation: You bump into someone, and their drink spills.

options.reply: Perfect! Saying sorry and helping is the best. 🌟
Accidents happen! 💜 But saying sorry helps them feel better.
Good start! Adding “I'm sorry” makes it even better. 😊

rounds.situation: Your friend wants to play a different game than you.

options.text: Let's play yours first, then mine!
options.reply: Great idea! Taking turns is fair. 🔄
Hmm, your friend might feel left out. 💜 Taking turns is a good idea.
That's OK too! Sometimes we want to play alone. 💜

rounds.situation: You don't understand what the teacher said.

options.reply: Yes! Asking helps you learn. That's smart! 🧠
A calmer voice works better. 😊 Try “Can you say it again, please?”
That's OK, but asking is a great way to learn! 🙋

rounds.situation: A new kid comes to your class.

options.text: Hi! Do you want to sit with me?
options.reply: So kind! The new kid will feel welcome. 🌟
Hmm, being new is scary. 💜 A friendly “hi” helps a lot.
A wave is a great start! 👋

options.text: Good game! Can we play again?
options.reply: Great sport! Everyone wants to play with a good sport! 🏆
Losing is hard! 💜 Try taking a breath and saying “Good game!”
That's a calm way to take it! 😊
